eval_instructions: Test against agents that are NOT yet M365-integrated across three languages: Node.js (LangChain/OpenAI/Claude), .NET AgentFramework, and Python AgentFramework. Requires .a365-workspace-detection.json to be present (written by a365-setup). The skill must WRAP existing LLM code, not replace it. For Node.js verify: (1) index.ts has CloudAdapter + authorizeJWT + /api/health + /api/messages, (2) agent.ts has AgentApplication with message/notification/InstallationUpdate handlers, (3) client.ts has getClient() factory wrapping the LLM, (4) ToolingManifest.json exists (empty), (5) core @microsoft/agents-hosting, @microsoft/agents-a365-runtime, @microsoft/agents-a365-notifications packages in package.json, (6) tsconfig has module: node16. For .NET verify: (1) Program.cs has AddAgent<T> + /api/messages + /api/health, (2) agent class extends AgentApplication with dual isAgenticOnly registrations, (3) .csproj has Microsoft.Agents.A365.Notifications, (4) appsettings.json has AgentApplication + TokenValidation + Connections. For Python verify: (1) host_agent_server.py has CloudAdapterAiohttp + /api/messages + /api/health + on_agent_notification, (2) agent.py implements AgentInterface with process_user_message and handle_agent_notification_activity, (3) agent_interface.py exists, (4) pyproject.toml has microsoft_agents_a365_notifications + microsoft_agents_a365_runtime + microsoft-agents-hosting-aiohttp. The skill runs instrument-observability (Phase 9.5) automatically as part of the AI Teammate package. add-workiq-tools (Phase 9.6) is optional — the user is asked and can accept or skip. The skill ends at Phase 10 (Final Summary) suggesting test-local as the next step (and add-workiq-tools if it was skipped).
